item.title: Analyzing Cyber Internet Usage and its Association With Physical Urban Functions: A Case Study in Macau
item.description: Transactions in GIS, Volume 30, Issue 6, September 2026.
item.dc:description: ABSTRACT The growing integration of digital technologies into daily life has increased the need to understand urban functions from both physical and cyber perspectives. While previous urban function research has primarily relied on physical‐space indicators, relatively little attention has been paid to how locations are utilized in cyber space. This study investigates cyber Internet usage and its association with physical urban functions using large‐scale public Wi‐Fi data collected from 1345 Wi‐Fi access points in Macau. A multidimensional framework was developed to characterize cyber Internet usage through three dimensions: traffic volume, connection count, and connection duration. Based on these dimensions, 30 indicators were constructed to capture usage intensity, intraday distribution, interday variation, long‐term trends, and temporal periodicity. Statistical analysis, Random Forest classification, and SHAP‐based model interpretation were employed to examine differences in cyber Internet usage across Food and Beverage, Public Service, and Retail functions and to evaluate the contribution of different cyber Internet usage characteristics to urban function classification. The results show that 28 of the 30 indicators differ significantly among urban function categories. The Random Forest model achieved an accuracy of 0.61, outperforming the baseline classifier and indicating that cyber Internet usage provides meaningful information for distinguishing urban functions. SHAP analysis further demonstrates that temporal indicators, particularly those describing intraday activity distributions and interday variations, contribute more to urban function differentiation than overall activity intensity. In addition, the relationships between cyber Internet usage and urban functions are function‐specific and partially nonlinear. Overall, this study extends urban function research by incorporating a cyber dimension and demonstrates the value of public Wi‐Fi data for understanding interactions between cyber activities and urban space.

item.title: Integrating ANN, CNN and Superpixel‐Based Graph Convolution in Ecologically Constrained Urban Growth Modeling: The ANN‐SGCCA Approach
item.description: Transactions in GIS, Volume 30, Issue 6, September 2026.
item.dc:description: ABSTRACT In urban growth modeling, spatial zoning represents a fundamental mechanism for implementing ecological constraints by delineating areas in which urban development is prohibited or restricted. However, existing urban growth simulation studies face two major limitations: (1) they often overlook the heterogeneous neighborhood spatial interactions of ecological factors across multiple scales, and (2) deep learning algorithms remain underutilized in capturing these complex interactions and learning ecological constraints. To address these gaps, we propose a novel approach for calibrating ecological constraints in urban growth modeling. The proposed ANN‐SGCCA model first derives development suitability using artificial neural networks (ANNs), while CNNs and superpixel‐based graph convolutional networks (SGCNs) are employed to extract ecological constraints at the pixel and superpixel levels, respectively. We applied this model to simulate urban dynamics in Quanzhou, a coastal city in southeastern China. The results demonstrate that the ANN‐SGCCA model significantly outperforms the traditional ANN‐CA model, with relative improvements of 28.1% and 29.3% in mean Figure of Merit (FoM) and Recall‐based Efficacy, respectively. Moreover, compared with the current ANN‐CCA model, which relies on CNNs to derive ecological constraints, our model achieves relative improvements of 11.1% and 13.5%, demonstrating its superior ability to characterize spatial ecological constraints. This new model has implications for simulating urban dynamics under complex ecological resource constraints.

ABSTRACT

In urban growth modeling, spatial zoning represents a fundamental mechanism for implementing ecological constraints by delineating areas in which urban development is prohibited or restricted. However, existing urban growth simulation studies face two major limitations: (1) they often overlook the heterogeneous neighborhood spatial interactions of ecological factors across multiple scales, and (2) deep learning algorithms remain underutilized in capturing these complex interactions and learning ecological constraints. To address these gaps, we propose a novel approach for calibrating ecological constraints in urban growth modeling. The proposed ANN-SGCCA model first derives development suitability using artificial neural networks (ANNs), while CNNs and superpixel-based graph convolutional networks (SGCNs) are employed to extract ecological constraints at the pixel and superpixel levels, respectively. We applied this model to simulate urban dynamics in Quanzhou, a coastal city in southeastern China. The results demonstrate that the ANN-SGCCA model significantly outperforms the traditional ANN-CA model, with relative improvements of 28.1% and 29.3% in mean Figure of Merit (FoM) and Recall-based Efficacy, respectively. Moreover, compared with the current ANN-CCA model, which relies on CNNs to derive ecological constraints, our model achieves relative improvements of 11.1% and 13.5%, demonstrating its superior ability to characterize spatial ecological constraints. This new model has implications for simulating urban dynamics under complex ecological resource constraints.
